document.title: Untrusted X-User and X-Source headers can forge management audit attribution

publisher.contact_details: Email tony@defendics.com and follow the disclosure process in https://github.com/tonylturner/containd/blob/main/SECURITY.md
publisher.issuing_authority: The containd project publishes a CSAF VEX document for each release and CSAF security advisories for confirmed vulnerabilities that affect the containd codebase, official container images, and directly maintained release artifacts.
publisher.name: containd project

revision_history.summary: Initial publication of affected management versions and the 0.1.42 fix.
Add the X-Source audit-provenance vulnerability, affected through 0.1.42 and fixed in 0.1.43.

notes.text: Management API requests could use an untrusted X-User header as the audit actor in lab mode or static-token sessions, and an untrusted X-Source header to forge the audit source label. The X-User issue also affected lab-mode learn-suggestion review; normal authenticated user sessions were unaffected. The X-Source issue affected audit records persisted and forwarded to syslog, but the source label was not used for authorization decisions.

vulnerabilities.title: Management actor attribution trusts X-User in lab and static-token sessions

notes.text: The audit middleware read X-User into the actor context, and audit logging also fell back to the request header. Lab mode (CONTAIND_LAB_MODE=1) and static API token authentication did not overwrite that context with an authenticated actor. A caller with the privileges needed for a management operation could attribute its audit record to a forged identity; lab-mode learn-suggestion requests also forwarded that actor for review. This is an attribution integrity flaw, not a bypass of the operation permission checks. Normal JWT user sessions set the authenticated username and were unaffected.

notes.title: Version evidence
notes.text: Commit a707237b introduced the X-User reads. Every repository tag from the first containing tag, v0.1.2-beta, through v0.1.41 contains the reads and lacks the fix. v0.1.42 contains bdf001dc through merge 9a0614a5: authentication sets the actor for lab and static-token sessions, and the audit header fallback is removed.

notes.title: Product and operating-mode scope
notes.text: This advisory concerns the management API of the containd management product. The supported standalone containd-engine deployment uses engine mode and does not register the management API. Both images contain a multi-mode executable; this exclusion is not a claim that overriding the engine image command to mgmt or all makes management API behavior impossible.

notes.title: Scope of the fix
notes.text: This revision covers only X-User actor attribution. It does not claim that other caller-controlled audit metadata is fixed.

remediations.details: Upgrade the management product to containd 0.1.42 or later.

Disable lab mode and use normal authenticated JWT user sessions instead of static API tokens. If an affected authentication mode must remain in use, strip the incoming X-User header at a trusted reverse proxy and prevent clients from bypassing that proxy to reach management directly. Header stripping prevents this spoofing but does not supply a verified per-user actor for static-token or lab requests, and historical lab review operations may be unavailable without an actor.

vulnerabilities.title: Management audit source attribution trusts X-Source

notes.text: The management API copied the caller-controlled X-Source request header into the source field of persisted audit records. Audit records are also exported to syslog, so a client able to reach the management API could forge their source label in stored and forwarded audit metadata. The source value is not used in authorization decisions; the demonstrated impact is limited to integrity of audit provenance.

notes.title: Version evidence
notes.text: Commit 695d3deb introduced the X-Source reads; v0.1.37 is the first release tag containing that commit. Inspection of every release tag from v0.1.37 through v0.1.42 found the header copied into audit context and/or used as the auditLog fallback. Commit ba9535f3 removes both client-header paths and sets the source server-side; this fix is included in 0.1.43.

notes.title: CVSS scoring
notes.text: No CVSS 3.1 score is assigned. The demonstrated impact is integrity of audit metadata only, but the privilege level required to reach a management API operation varies by configuration and the available evidence does not justify a single vector.

remediations.details: Upgrade the management product to containd 0.1.43 or later.
Strip the incoming X-Source header at a trusted reverse proxy and prevent clients from bypassing that proxy to reach the management API directly.
